title: Sharp $L^p$-estimates for wave equation on $ax+b$ groups: the sharp polynomial-in-time lower bound (Proposition 5.1)
author: Yunxiang Wang, Lixin Yan
work: Sharp $L^p$-estimates for wave equation on $ax+b$ groups
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the proposition printed as Proposition 5.1 of "Sharp L^p-estimates for wave equation on ax+b groups" (source0.tex lines 989--994, source label prop5.1), delivered together with the article's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 995--1088 (94 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The proposition is the sharpness half of the article's main theorem, and the authors announce it as a stronger statement than the sharpness assertion of Theorem 1.1: for every 1<=p<=infty, every t>0 and every real alpha, the operator sin(t sqrt L)/sqrt L is bounded below from the Sobolev space L^p_alpha(G) to L^p(G) by C t. The proof is complete inside the retained span: it moves to the (s,y) coordinates in which the right Haar measure is Lebesgue measure and the Riemannian metric becomes ds^2+e^{-2s}dy^2, builds the explicit cut-off q_t supported in a slab { -10t-5 <= s <= -2t-1, |y_j| <= 2 }, proves the Sobolev bound ||(Id+L)^{alpha}(q_t)||_{L^p} <= C(1+t)^{1/p} by splitting the power of the operator and using the L^p-boundedness of the negative-order part together with the multiplier estimates of Mueller--Thiele and Stein, and then uses the unit-speed propagation property of the wave equation to show that sin(t sqrt L)/sqrt L (q_t) equals t on the smaller set S_t, which yields the lower bound C t (1+t)^{1/p} and hence the proposition. It is not a routine exercise: the proof has to combine the explicit geometry of the ax+b group, the exponential-volume behaviour of the sets involved, a multiplier calculus on a non-unimodular group and a finite-speed-of-propagation argument, and it produces the sharp growth rate that the introduction of the article advertises. Rated H3 because the delivered unit is the sharpness part of the paper's resolution of the Mueller--Thiele conjecture, and because the construction and the propagation argument are research-level analysis rather than anything in an ordinary PhD qualifying syllabus.
